sections.h2: Your options for selling in Stonecrest
sections.html:
Sellers in this city end up choosing between a listing agent, a do-it-yourself sale, and a quick cash purchase where the investor deals with repairs. The right pick follows the condition of the roof and kitchen, your loan payoff, your moving date, and who is living there now.

  • A listing agent fits a tidy house and an owner with time to wait.
  • Going solo saves the commission, though you take on pricing, disclosure forms and haggling.
  • Ask for cash bids if the house has deferred repairs, tax arrears or a probate matter hanging over it.

Stonecrest sits inside DeKalb County, so county offices handle property tax on every parcel, while the city keeps its own permit and business license staff. Knowing who answers what saves phone calls later.

The city is young. Incorporation passed by vote on November 8, 2016, and the city began operating on July 10, 2017. Its own staff cover zoning, code enforcement, business licenses and building permits. The county still provides police, fire, road upkeep and sanitation. The city set its first millage rate in 2020, so ask the DeKalb Tax Commissioner what city levy, if any, appears on your bill.

The estimated population is 61,337, in 20,995 households, and owners occupy 56.3 percent of the homes. With nearly half the homes rented, investors planning a rental belong in your buyer pool.

sections.h2: What buyers like about the area
sections.html:
Retail in the city centers on the Mall at Stonecrest, ringed by medical, office and hotel parcels around it and DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale as the main hospital. Interstate 20 and State Routes 124 and 278 lead toward downtown Atlanta and Hartsfield-Jackson airport. Two industrial areas hold some of the larger local employers, so a buyer who works at one of them may want a short drive.

Outdoor space is the other draw. The Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area covers 2,550 acres of exposed granite, wetlands, streams, lakes and forest linked by trails, and Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Park and Panola Mountain State Park sit nearby. A listing or a cash pitch can mention the drive to the mall corridor or the trailheads, since those are the things people ask about first.

The August mailing is addressed to the January 1 titleholder, and a second copy goes to a newer owner if there is one. Choose between two payments (September 30 and November 15) or one payment by September 30. For mailed payments, a clerk's hand-canceled postmark dated by the deadline is the proof the county accepts. A meter stamp or kiosk label will not count. Miss the date and the penalty is 5 percent.

The county does not mail bills to lenders. Owners with escrow should ask the servicer to confirm the payment went out before listing.

On a single-family home, the county prints a yearly sanitation assessment for trash pickup of $362.30 on the same bill.

For a sale that closes after January 1, the county's advice to the buyer is to read the closing statement or ask the attorney, lender or escrow agent who owes the bill. Any balance remains a charge on the land itself. Request an itemized tax line on the settlement statement so both sides see the split.

Overdue taxes get paid from your sale proceeds at the closing table. Cash buyers rarely balk at this, which is why owners behind on taxes often start with cash bids.

DeKalb's homestead test asks three things: the house is your main residence on January 1, your Georgia license or ID shows that address, and your vehicles are registered there. Filing closes in mid-July. An exemption is never granted on its own and does not move to the buyer, who must file a fresh application. Once granted, an exemption puts an assessment freeze on county taxes that may limit increases, though it does not touch school, city or state taxes.

  • Special exemptions with income limits exist for homeowners 62 and older, disabled homeowners, former service members rated 100 percent disabled, and some surviving spouses.
  • From the date of the notice you have 45 days to appeal. Fax and email filings get rejected, so deliver it by hand or mail.
  • You can take the case to the Board of Equalization (free), to nonbinding arbitration ($217 plus a certified appraisal), or, for non-homestead property valued over $500,000, to a hearing officer.
  • An appeal still open when bills print means you pay on a temporary value, typically the lower of last year's final figure or 85 percent of this year's.

The county appraises at 100 percent of market value and taxes 40 percent of that. The Property Appraisal Department is at 325 Swanton Way in Decatur, and the Tax Commissioner's central office is at 4380 Memorial Drive in Decatur.

Have the parcel number and the property address ready, plus your most recent assessment notice if you have one. The Property Appraisal Department answers value questions, and the Tax Commissioner's office answers billing and payment questions. Keeping those two straight shortens most calls. If you plan to dispute a value, start counting the 45 days from the date on the notice, not from the day it reaches your mailbox.

Georgia's recording rule is simple: no transfer tax, no recorded deed. Sellers carry the cost unless the contract moves it. The rate is posted on the Department of Revenue's transfer tax page, and the PT-61 declaration goes in electronically from you or your closing office.

If you doubt that your transfer is taxable, the Clerk of Superior Court in the county can answer. Most closing attorneys file the form and subtract the tax from what you receive.

sections.h2: Checklist before you accept an offer
sections.html:
1. Pull together your deed, DeKalb parcel number and latest assessment notice.
  2. Find out if a homestead exemption is on file and tell buyers it ends when you sell.
  3. Open the August bill and mark which installments you have paid.
  4. Order a payoff statement from your lender and a lien search through the closing attorney.
  5. Weigh each offer by the net you walk away with after transfer tax, repair credits and the closing date.

With cash there is no buyer mortgage and no lender appraisal, so two usual causes of delay disappear. The price is often lower in exchange, so keep two or three bids in front of you.

faqs.a: Yes. Voters created it on November 8, 2016, and it began operating on July 10, 2017. The city runs zoning, permits and business licenses, while DeKalb County bills property tax and handles public safety.

faqs.q: When are DeKalb County property tax installments due?
faqs.a: Two payments are due, September 30 and November 15. A single full payment must be in by September 30. Late payments carry a 5 percent penalty, and the postmark rules are strict.

faqs.q: Does my DeKalb homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. It stays with you. The buyer files a new application and has to meet the January 1 ownership and residency tests.

faqs.q: What is the DeKalb appeal deadline?
faqs.a: The limit is 45 days from the date the notice was mailed. Hand-deliver the appeal or mail it so it is postmarked in time, since fax and email filings are refused.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: Your closing statement should say. DeKalb sends one bill to the January 1 owner and another to the new owner, and it points buyers to the closing attorney or escrow agent for the answer. Any unpaid amount remains with the property.
